title: mainnet-addresses.ts carries 0x0 placeholders for Kendu and NudgeStreamer that are type-indistinguishable from real addresses, because the ContractAddresses interface is regenerated from ANVIL data with every field a required plain string
description: `generate-ts-addresses.js` regenerates `addresses.ts`'s `ContractAddresses` interface from local.json — i.e. from ANVIL data — emitting `${name}: string;` for every one of the 57 keys, all required, all plain `string`. The hand-maintained `mainnet-addresses.ts` is annotated `: ContractAddresses`, so a purely local mock addition forces a placeholder into the mainnet address book. Story-073 commit d241e61 did exactly that for `Kendu` (:64) and `NudgeStreamer` (:131), both `0x0000…0000`. Nothing in the type system, the file, or the :3001 API distinguishes a placeholder from a real address.
impact: A mainnet script sourcing `NudgeStreamer` or `Kendu` from this file gets address(0). IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the prior framing: this does NOT produce a silent mis-wire on the donor path — all six donors reject `setNudgeStreamer(address(0))` explicitly, and `setNudgeTokenWhitelist(address(0), true)` reverts `BatchMint__ZeroNudgeToken`, so those legs fail LOUDLY at deploy time. The one silent consumer is `BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer`, which has no guard (see DEV-03). The residual risk is therefore (a) that one silent leg and (b) a general operator-trust problem: the file's zero addresses read as data, not as 'not yet deployed'.
attackPath: No attack path. generate-ts-addresses.js:57 regenerates the ContractAddresses interface from local.json - i.e. from ANVIL data - emitting `${name}: string;` for all 57 keys, all required and all plain string. mainnet-addresses.ts is annotated `: ContractAddresses`, so a purely local mock addition forces a placeholder into the mainnet address book (story-073 commit d241e61 did exactly that for Kendu :64 and NudgeStreamer :131).
evidence: server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts:64 `Kendu: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"`, :131 `NudgeStreamer: "0x00…00"`. server/generate-ts-addresses.js:57 `lines.push(\`  ${name}: string;\`)`. Live run: addresses.ts regenerated with 57 required string fields; the :3001 API serves both `Kendu` and `NudgeStreamer` with no mock/placeholder marker and zero `Mock`-prefixed keys.
recommendation: Introduce a branded or optional type for not-yet-deployed entries (e.g. `NudgeStreamer?: string` or a `type NotDeployed = "0x0"` union) so the compiler distinguishes them, or split the interface into a mainnet-required core and an anvil-only extension so local mock additions stop type-gating the mainnet address book. At minimum, add a runtime guard in any mainnet script: `require(addr != address(0), "<name> not deployed")` at the point of read.

severityRationale: LOW, matching the auditor's proposal, and I want to record WHY it is not Medium so no reader collapses it upward. The finding's own impact text carries the correct bounding fact: this does NOT produce a silent mis-wire on the donor path. All six donors reject setNudgeStreamer(address(0)) explicitly (verified this run at top-level HEAD), and setNudgeTokenWhitelist(address(0), true) reverts BatchMint__ZeroNudgeToken - so those legs fail LOUDLY at deploy time. There is exactly ONE silent consumer, BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.setNudgeStreamer, and that consumer is already charged at Medium as DEV-03. Rating DEV-06 Medium as well would DOUBLE-COUNT one impact across two findings, which is precisely the overstatement this pipeline rejects. DEV-06's independent residual is the operator-trust problem: the file's zero addresses read as data rather than as 'not yet deployed', and nothing in the type system, the file, or the :3001 API distinguishes them. That is a genuine Law-3 footgun (a competent operator would be surprised that the mainnet address book is type-gated by anvil-derived output) and it sustains a Low. Correct framing for the report: DEV-06 is the loaded gun, DEV-03 is the one barrel with no safety.

parkedItemsCarriedForward.title: ERC4626YieldStrategy.previewRedeem / previewDeposit view passthroughs still STATICCALL the underlying vault — the story-060 / YS-01 Tokemak fix is one-directional
parkedItemsCarriedForward.sourceVerification: Read against the TOP-LEVEL submodule HEAD lib/reflax-yield-vault (not a nested stale pin). :73-75 `return vault.previewDeposit(assets);` and :83-85 `return vault.previewRedeem(shares);`, both declared `external view` => Solidity emits STATICCALL. Twenty lines below, :110-115 credits principal via `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` with an in-source comment naming the exact hazard: 'Use convertToAssets (NOT previewRedeem): convertToAssets is ERC4626-mandated STATICCALL-safe, whereas some real vaults (e.g. Tokemak Autopools) mutate state inside previewRedeem and revert with StateChangeDuringStaticCall when called as an external view.' The authors therefore knew the hazard and hardened ONE call site.
parkedItemsCarriedForward.whyItMatters: Against a real Tokemak Autopool these two views revert for every caller, always; against MockAutoDOLA (plain un-overridden OZ ERC4626) they return a clean number, always. The local rig therefore reports green on the exact behaviour that already bricked this project's YS-swap suite. Blast radius today is UI/keeper reads (no first-party on-chain caller found), which is why this is parked for triage rather than asserted as a Medium.

MockAutoDOLA._updateYield() mints assets into the vault BEFORE super._deposit mints shares, so convertToAssets(sharesReceived) > amount and creditedPrincipal at :115 can EXCEED the deposited amount — the precise opposite of that line's stated intent. Any local invariant asserting 'principal is never over-credited' passes VACUOUSLY. Flagged because a vacuous-harness result is a known repeat failure mode in this repo.
